item.title: US: Additional charge filed against Meghan Markle's father
item.description:
A California grand jury approved a two-count indictment against Thomas Markle, 82, the father of Meghan Markle, Prince Harry's wife, for possessing illegal material depicting the abuse of minors.
Markle was arrested in Florida earlier this month and initially faced only one charge. With the addition of the second charge, he faces a maximum sentence of 40 years in prison if convicted. Markle denies the allegations against him.

item.title: Turkey: Five military personnel killed in helicopter crash
item.description:
The Turkish Ministry of Defense announced this evening that five military personnel, including two pilots and three technical staff members, were killed in the crash of a Turkish Air Force AS-532 helicopter during a training flight in the Eskisehir region.
Rescue forces have reached the remains of the helicopter. The circumstances of the crash are being investigated. This is the second fatal military helicopter accident in Turkey in less than two weeks.

item.description: Attorney Yair Nehorai, a leading opponent of growing religious influence, calls for ending efforts to draft haredim and disbanding the IDF's haredi units. He tells Arutz Sheva why he believes mass enlistment threatens Israel's liberal character.

item.title: 47-year-old woman with no underlying conditions in critical condition due to flu complications
item.description:
A 47-year-old woman with no known underlying medical conditions is hospitalized in critical condition at Meir Medical Center in Kfar Saba after developing complications from influenza A.
The woman was rushed to the hospital suffering from multiple organ failure. She was sedated, placed on a ventilator, and connected to an ECMO machine.
The hospital noted that the woman had been vaccinated approximately one week before falling ill, emphasizing that it takes about two weeks following vaccination for optimal protection to develop.

item.title: "Bring about real change": Maj. (res.) Yitzhaki Glick's plan to resolve the draft issue
item.description: In an Arutz Sheva studio interview, Maj. (res.) Yitzhaki Glick, an attorney, says Bismuth's and Liberman's draft plans fall short. He proposes universal service, a small Torah study quota and a Zionist government not reliant on haredi parties.

item.title: Suspected stun grenade thrown at Eilat home; no injuries
item.description:
Police have opened an investigation following a suspicion that a stun grenade was thrown at a house in Eilat. There were no injuries in the incident.
Police forces and forensic investigators collected evidence at the scene, and the background is suspected to be a criminal incident.
